utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. First of all, I would like to thank you for your suggestion that the colour version of the photographs should be obtained. That was our suggestion, and you have been of great assistance. I just want to address certain key issues raised by my learned colleague Mr. Re. He mentioned the issue of the witnesses and the shortcomings in their testimony. I dealt with this issue at the very beginning of this case. I said that from a criminal point of view, the witness is the least adequate form of evidence. I provided an example from the Middle Ages. Thousand or even a million people were sentenced to death by burning on the basis of testimony from witnesses, and their evidence was very consistent. We can say that we're not in the Middle Ages, but what happened in Bosnia, unfortunately it didn't even happen in the Middle Ages, especially with regard to portraying the truth and portraying various inhumane acts. So we would like to request that the Trial Chamber bear this in mind, and especially to bear in mind the conclusions in the Celebici case with regard to certain imperfections, and if I'm not wrong, with regard to the verbal ambiguity. I think that's the correct term. In such cases a judgement cannot be delivered against the accused. If there are any doubts about a witness, this shouldn't be prejudicial to the accused; quite the contrary. The baton was mentioned with a spring, and in our appeal we said that Mrkalj Edin, the witness Mrkalj Edin said that on the 16th of June 1992 - and that is the day that Fadil Avdagic mentioned as being the date on which Becir Medunjanin died, because he was a witness - on that date he was released home and he remembers that date with great precision. Other witnesses have no doubt as to whether it was the 15th or the 16th. Mrkalj Edin says the 16th of June. In Omarska, In the hangar in Omarska, Zoran Vokic -- another Zoran, not Zigic but Vokic, the names are similar -- a man with long hair, an earring. He had fair hair and had the same sort of baton, a metal baton, and 20 metres from the "white house" he used this baton to beat Mrkalj Edin. This description: He was tall, fair, had an earring. This corresponds Fadil Avdagic's description of Zigic: Tall, fair, with an earring. We saw in the expert's testimony that Zigic never was fair or tall. Avdagic said that on that occasion Zigic had fair hair -- or rather, yellowish-reddish dyed hair. A face with yellowish-reddish hair killed Becir Medunjanin. An eyewitness, Fadil Avdagic, made this statement and the judgement is based on this statement. This witness says that he was a metre or a metre and a half away from the place where this event occurred. KV3 and KV4 said today that this person had dark hair. Witness T said that Fadil Avdagic, whose head he was holding in his hands, this witness also said that the person had dark hair. These inconsistencies aren't just slight or minor inconsistencies. We heard from my colleague that Witness KV3 recognised Zigic to be the person who arrived in Omarska in a van. This fact suits us, the fact that he recognised Zigic. We link it up to the fact that was also stated, that that person was in no way connected to the murder of Becir Medunjanin, and this was stated very unambiguously. He said that he didn't know his name, but he said that he knew Zigic's name and that he knew him well before Omarska. Certain doubts of today's witness: For example, he said that he thought that he -- that two persons were Zigic. I don't think the witness said who the other person was, but he made two mistakes. He was mistaken in the case of Zigic and in the case of Kos. As he himself said, he was in charge of the shift. I wouldn't want anything to be misunderstood by Mr. Re. I think that they have acted in a correct manner. But I would just like to say that the witnesses have consideration for them. I was on that side. People went there and they were very grateful for everything that was done and I want to -- to inform you of the difference of the responses provided by the witness for the Prosecution and for the Defence. They don't want to offend the Prosecution, and there were certain inconsistencies. But I don't think it's important. What is important is that the witness quite unambiguously stated that Zigic was not a participant. We're just mentioning witnesses here who we heard over the last few days. We're not mentioning the testimony of other witnesses, at least 10 other witnesses or more than 10 witnesses who were sure that Zigic wasn't there and that he was not a participant, and we're not mentioning inconsistencies in the testimony of these witnesses and the other witnesses. We'd be grateful if this Appeals Chamber applied the standards from the Celebici case, especially the standards that were applied in the case of the accused Delic. The witnesses for the Prosecution were dismissed for certain inconsistencies, certain errors that were mentioned with regard to other facts. We would like the standards from the Kupreskic case to be applied, as I have already said. And finally, we think that the Chamber, regardless of all the positions -- all the opinions I have expressed, has the discretion to assess the situation, the case, and it should be consistent with the Celebici judgement and the sentencing judgement. I think they themselves reached certain conclusions. They didn't bind their own hands. And it is first necessary to establish certain factual truths, and also one must establish that one can't be accused on the basis of contradictory evidence. Witness T - and you will read his statement in detail; he's a key witness for the judgement - compare what Witness T said and what Fadil Avdagic said. These are two witnesses. Compare that with what's been said today. Compare that with the statement of Azedin Oklopcic, who was Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond quoted on 27 occasions in the judgement. He is believed and it was on his testimony that Zigic was also accused. But he also says that Zigic didn't participate in the murder of Becir Medunjanin. But he wasn't believed here. Abdulah Brkic, we heard that he was present in the "white house" today. He knows Zigic. He was quoted on nine occasions in the judgement. He accuses Zigic in three or four places, but he also explicitly states that Zigic didn't murder Becir Medunjanin and that he didn't participate in that. Why isn't he believed, if everything else is believed? We would like to know the reasons for which this witness is not believed. I don't want to go over innumerable arguments. I think I am a little confused, not because that is my nature but because I have at least between 100 and 200 other inconsistencies in mind and other matters that are not clear with regard to all the charges against Mr. Zigic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Re, do you have the colour photo board now?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have one of them; that's Exhibit KV -- sorry, DA5, which was the one shown to DV -- sorry, KV4. If I can produce that to the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: So that one is already part of the record, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Without comparing it -- there were some photo boards in the trial record, but without comparing that exact one with what I suspect are Exhibits 31 --/129A to D, I don't know. But that -- that is the original of the one shown to KV4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, do you agree to it? Mr. Stojanovic, is that a photo board in which you're interested?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I see it, please. Yes, that's the one. I don't know whether we could obtain the same thing for Witness KV3, but this is certainly the one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I thought that Mr. Re wanted to say something, or perhaps not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You'd like to say something, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. I've just produced -- the first one I produced was the Exhibit DA5. I've now been given a copy of DA2, which was the one shown to Witness KV3, who testified yesterday. And I can also produce the original. This is the original with the original notes as well -- to the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Could they be passed to Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe it's correct, but just a moment. I have a very bad copy. That's it. Yes. [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: My colleagues on my left are content. Then we shall proceed. Mr. Fila, do you have any remarks?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, very briefly, two or three sentences only, if I may. First of all, the additional evidence does not directly affect Mr. Radic, but indirectly everything that happened in Omarska affects everyone. And according to your judgement, there is not a direct relationship between the victim and the torturer, but it applies to all round. That is why after these three days I still stand by my submission that the judgement should be reviewed in line with Rule 117(C) and that there should be a re-trial. But I must repeat that I personally cannot agree with the test applied by my learned friend Re to the effect that no one reasonable would pass such a judgement and that that would mean that the Trial Chamber was unreasonable. That is not what I mean. That is excessive, and I would never say of any individual Judge that his decision was unreasonable. I haven't said that in 41 years, and I don't think I should change my principles. That is as far as that is concerned. Secondly, I wish once again to express my gratitude and to convey my personal feelings to this Chamber that I feel privileged and honoured to act as Defence counsel in this Chamber. Up to now I have had that opportunity to act as Defence counsel in the presence of only one member of this Trial Chamber. And thirdly, that there's an identical saying among our three peoples which says that "The end of every act is the most important." And in your case, it is your judgement; and that, I expect that climax or that final act to come as soon as possible because it is now almost four years that we have been waiting for that. I will use another proverb. I don't know how it translates, and that is "When something is done in haste, it cannot be good." However, this is not hasty enough to become inappropriate. I would appeal to The Chamber to make their determination as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have nothing to add nor to ask. We have said everything that we had to say, and this part of the proceedings doesn't affect Mr. Prcac, but it does affect all of us. As colleague Fila has said, we have drawn attention to certain formal omissions in the trial itself, and if those errors were admitted, then the judgement should be changed; but if not, then we feel that the factual basis of this judgement has not been established or has erroneously been established and not in accordance with the standard that the guilt be established beyond any reasonable doubt and that that standard cannot be said to apply in this case at all. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you indeed. We're very grateful for all the assistance we've had from the bar, and I want to say a special word about the colour photo board. Mr. Stojanovic, you can be assured that the Bench will consider very carefully the photo board, the colour photo board, and we also thank the Prosecution for supplying it at short notice. Now, with that, I have to say that we will reserve our judgement and we will give that as soon as possible. Meanwhile, I would say this, that we would now adjourn these proceedings, and after five minutes my colleague Judge Weinberg de Roca will return to take the Status Conference which should be held. And I think it is referred to in one of the papers. So Judge Weinberg de Roca will reside over the Status Conference. Meanwhile, we adjourn these proceedings. We thank you all, and a judgement will be delivered sometime in the autumn. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: to be followed by a Status Conference.
